notes.text: This portrait manuscript is written over the reverse of a machine listing. The pale blue reversed type is excluded as show-through. The lighter bottom-left 37 is retained as foliation with its hand unassigned. No printed dates or source-page sequence are inferred from H’s editorial comments.

The parenthesized distinctes is a raised addition linked to orbites in item b. It is not dimension1; complexe lies on the preceding baseline. The square-torsor identification is also interlinear, with two visible comma strokes retained around the addition.

The page studies a nonidentity holomorphic involution of a sphere preserving five marked points. A Möbius involution has two fixed points. Decomposing a five-element invariant set into fixed points and two-element orbits leaves exactly one fixed point and two free orbits. Marking the fixed point called infinity and calling the other zero gives the multiplicative-torsor description used in item a.

After those two fixed points are placed at infinity and zero, the involution is multiplication by −1. Squaring identifies its two-element orbits on the nonzero line with points of the square torsor. Thus item b’s unordered pair of distinct orbits corresponds to an unordered pair of distinct nonzero square-torsor points.

The page uses wedge notation for a symmetric torsor product, as its explicit xi-wedge-eta=eta-wedge-xi indicates. In a compatible coordinate, e is the nonzero product xi eta in the fourth tensor power. A choice of e gives the fourth-root reduction to mu4; the two square roots in the square line give the plus/minus basis called a bibase. Relative to either member of that pair, the coordinate of xi+eta is determined up to sign. These are the interpretations checked; an alternating exterior-product convention is not imposed.

If the uncertain sign inside the first parentheses is plus, the computed identity (xi+eta)^2−4xi eta=(xi−eta)^2 gives the distinctness criterion over C. The manuscript visibly writes a wedge in the later product and a peaked, unresolved wedge/plus sign inside the parentheses. Its cancelled expanded expression is compatible with the identity if the uncertain first exponent is2. These algebraic checks do not resolve the manuscript signs or the cancelled strokes.

The sum target is written with a t/T-like crossbar, not a clear L. If it denotes the previously defined T2=L2-star, the membership assertion has a counterexample: xi=1 and eta=−1 are distinct nonzero points, their product is−1 and their sum is0. The plus interpretation of the following condition gives4, and the product interpretation gives5 in these coordinates; either is nonzero. The appropriate ambient vector line would be L2. The literal ambiguous t/T form remains in the transcription.

In the fourth-root group notation the star is visibly below C, unlike the raised star just before it. The low placement is preserved as C_*. No further meaning or correction of this local star placement is imposed.

checks.outcome: Represent the nonidentity Möbius involution by a nonscalar invertible 2×2 matrix A. Its square is scalar. Over C its two distinct eigenvalues differ by sign, giving exactly two fixed projective directions; after placing them at0 and infinity the map is z↦−z. This checks the geometric fixed-point premise used on the page.

checks.outcome: Enumerating integer solutions of 5=f+2n with 0≤f≤2 and n≥0 returned only (f,n)=(1,2). This checks the fixed-point/orbit count conditional on the preceding geometric premise.

checks.outcome: For nonzero complex x and y, x²=y² iff y=x or y=−x. The squaring map therefore identifies exactly the ±1 orbits; distinct orbits give distinct nonzero points of the square line.

checks.who: GPT-6 Astra Pro; effort not exposed; run SP82_C13_148; reader B
checks.outcome: For e≠0, the roots of w⁴=e are nonzero and distinct because 4w³ does not vanish there; multiplication by the fourth roots of1 acts freely and transitively. In the square line, the two roots of v²=e differ by sign and are nonzero. Dividing the same vector sum by the two opposite bases changes its scalar coordinate by sign.

checks.outcome: SymPy expanded (x+y)²−4xy to x²−2xy+y², factored it as (x−y)², and returned0 for the difference between x²+y²−2xy and (x−y)². This checks the plus interpretation and tentative expanded algebra only; it does not settle the manuscript’s wedge/plus sign or cancelled handwriting.

checks.outcome: Substituting x=1,y=−1 gives product−1, sum0 and (x+y)²−4xy=4. Direct substitution also gives (xy)²−4xy=1+4=5. The sum therefore need not lie in the nonzero torsor under either reading of the separate uncertain sign.
